docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Install, update and troubleshoot Vega's FiveM scripts on Qbox, ESX and QBCore. The badges at the top of every script page show which frameworks it works with, and Browse by framework groups them.

Free scripts

Download from GitHub

Open source. Get the .zip from the script's latest release and install it like any resource.

Install a free script

Paid scripts

Buy in the store

Pay with Tebex, then download the script from portal.cfx.re under Granted Assets.

Install a paid script

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A FiveM server. OneSync is recommended; it's on by default on current servers.
  • The framework the script is built for.
  • The other resources listed on the script's page. ox_lib is recommended for the nicest notifications, and Qbox already includes it.

docs.title: Installing a script
docs.text:
1. Open the script's page in Docs and follow the latest release link.
  2. Download the .zip file under Assets.
  3. Unzip it into your server's resources folder.
  4. Add the script's items to your inventory (see below).
  5. Add ensure <resource name> to server.cfg, below your framework (see below).
  6. Restart the server.

docs.title: Installing a paid script
docs.text:
Paid scripts are protected with Cfx.re's asset escrow: they only start on servers whose license key belongs to the Cfx.re account that bought them.

  1. Buy the script in the store, logged in with the same Cfx.re account your server's license key belongs to.
  2. Log in at portal.cfx.re, open Assets and download the script from Granted Assets.
  3. Unzip it into your server's resources folder.
  4. Add the script's items to your inventory (see below).
  5. Add ensure <resource name> to server.cfg, below your framework (see below).
  6. Restart the server.

The config and language files stay open, so you can change every setting; the rest of the code is encrypted.

docs.title: server.cfg order
docs.text:
Resources start from top to bottom, so your framework and its libraries must come before any script that uses them.

ESXQBCoreQbox 
ensure oxmysql
ensure es_extended
ensure ox_lib          # optional
ensure <script name>

ensure oxmysql
ensure qb-core
ensure [qb]            # qb-inventory and other qb resources
ensure ox_lib          # optional
ensure <script name>

ensure oxmysql
ensure ox_lib
ensure qbx_core
ensure ox_inventory
ensure <script name>

If you installed with the Qbox txAdmin recipe, keep its order and add your scripts at the end.

Scripts that count police usually only count officers who are on duty. If a script says there aren't enough police, make sure the officers have clocked in.

docs.title: Updating a script
docs.text:
1. Check the Changelog on the script's page for anything new you need to set up. Free scripts: download the new release from GitHub. Paid scripts: download the new version from your Cfx.re portal.
  2. Back up your old config files (for example config/config.lua and config/config_server.lua).
  3. Delete the old script folder and put the new release in its place. Don't copy the new files over the old ones, because files can move between versions.
  4. Copy your changed values back into the new config file. Don't copy the old file over it, because new versions can add settings.
  5. Restart the script with ensure <resource name> in the server console, or restart the server.

docs.title: Finding errors
docs.text: If something doesn't work, look at the server console and the F8 console in game. Errors show the resource name, for example [tobs_bankrobbery]. Each script page has a Troubleshooting section for the common ones.

v1.0.1 Qbox · ESX · QBCore 11 languages GPL-3.0

Rob the Paleto Bay bank and all six Fleeca banks. Hack the security panel, open the vault and empty the trolleys before the police arrive.

docs.title: 1.0.1 · not released yet
docs.text:
Fixes and additions from playing 1.0.0 on a Qbox server. Tested in game on Qbox.

  • Inner gate at every bank, opened with its own minigame: gate in a bank's minigames, thermite by default. Its timer starts once the minigame is passed, and a failed try keeps the gate shut for another go
  • Two trolleys behind the gate (gateTrolleys), the right ones at Paleto and the Fleeca banks; a trolley behind the closed gate says so instead of doing nothing
  • Gold and diamond trolleys stand behind the gate and pay 44 gold bars or diamonds (one per grab); the loot counter counts them. Both items and their images are in install/. An item your inventory doesn't have is paid as cash
  • Grabbing ends with the money: the animation plays at the speed that empties the trolley in TOB.GrabTime, stops when it's paid out, and keeps counting while the game is alt-tabbed. Looting no longer sometimes does nothing
  • Emptied gold and diamond trolleys stay empty for every player
  • Paleto's vault door opens the right way (vaultTurn per bank)
  • Laptop hack: players are no longer pulled backwards (TOB.LaptopSceneForward)
  • 5 new languages: French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Polish and Italian (11 in total)
  • Every bank uses GTA's laptop and drill with tobs_minigames; Paleto has its own cash range ($40,000–60,000)
  • The end log names cash and items separately when a player got both

docs.title: 1.0.0 · 2026-09-28
docs.text:
The first release of tobs_bankrobbery as its own script: the server runs the whole heist, the framework code is shared with the other tobs_ scripts, and trolleys pay by the time spent grabbing. Plus GTA's own minigames and admin tools.

Tested in game on Qbox. QBCore and ESX are covered by the automated tests but haven't been played on a live server yet: please report anything that doesn't work there.

  • Qbox, ESX and QBCore in one resource, detected automatically (TOB.Framework). Qbox and QBCore count only on-duty police (TOB.PoliceOnDuty); items go through ox_inventory or qb-inventory
  • TOB.PoliceJob can be a list of jobs; /bankcoords prints positions for adding a bank; the install/ folder has the items for every inventory

  • The framework code (bridge/) is now shared with the other tobs_ scripts; TOB.PoliceGroup is gone

  • Security: every step and timer runs on the server, so cheaters can't skip the hack, open the vault early, loot before it's open, or keep it open. Grabbing faster pays nothing more, and players drill one deposit box at a time

  • Rewards: a full trolley pays TOB.TrolleyCash ($50,000–80,000) over TOB.GrabTime seconds. TOB.mincash, TOB.maxcash and TOB.MaxPiles are gone
  • Crew takeover when the robber disconnects
  • Any hacking minigame (TOB.HackMinigame)
  • ps-dispatch alerts out of the box, and SV.DispatchAlert for server-side dispatch
  • Events and exports for other resources
  • ox_lib text prompts instead of 3D text (TOB.Prompts)
  • Optional GPS tracker and dye pack in the loot
  • Marked bills with a worth value for QBCore / Qbox laundering
  • Cash and cooldown per bank (Fleeca trolleys now hold $30,000–50,000); banks moved to config/banks.lua
  • Trolleys spawned by the server with OneSync, and the gate uses GTA's door system
  • German, Swedish, Norwegian and Dutch
  • Players who join the server during a heist can loot it too
  • Minigames from tobs_minigames: GTA Online's hacking laptop and drilling screen, GTA V's safe dial and nine more, when tobs_minigames runs; per bank, with GTA's laptop and drill at Paleto
  • Admin tools: heist switch (/tobpause), test mode (/tobtest) and a health check (/tobcheck)
  • Every refusal says why, with the time left on cooldowns
  • Everyone in the bank hears the drill and the vault door
  • TOB.CardTime: time for the card, the laptop and the minigame (150 s instead of a fixed 90 s)
  • Cooldowns survive restarts; the countdown shows for the whole crew; the police blip lasts the whole heist; full pockets don't lose loot; a warning when OneSync is off

Updating from tobs_blaine: delete the old tobs_blaine folder, change ensure tobs_blaine to ensure tobs_bankrobbery in server.cfg, and copy your settings into the new config files. Set TOB.TrolleyCash instead of the old pile settings.

docs.text:
Feature What it does Setting Dispatch ps-dispatch works out of the box; any other dispatch script through a hook TOB.Dispatch, TOB.BuiltInPoliceAlert GPS tracker Some loot hides a tracker: police follow the robber on the map for a few minutes. Needs OneSync TOB.Tracker Dye pack Some trolleys burst into red smoke when the grab ends, ruining part of the money TOB.DyePack Using another dispatch script

Paste the alert call from its documentation into one of these. An error in your code doesn't stop the heist; it shows in the console.

Client-side dispatchServer-side dispatch

In config/config.lua, runs in the robber's game:

TOB.DispatchAlert = function(coords, bank)
    -- your dispatch script's alert, using coords
end

In config/config_server.lua, runs on the server:

SV.DispatchAlert = function(bank, coords, playerId, label)
    -- your dispatch script's server-side alert
end

With ps-dispatch, add camId = 1 to a bank in config/banks.lua to attach a camera.

Any function works as a minigame, as long as it returns true when the player passed:

TOB.HackMinigame = function(bank)
    return exports["my_minigame"]:Start(...) -- see that resource's documentation
end

With tobs_minigames running (ensure it above tobs_bankrobbery), a setting can also name one of its games: "hack", "drill", "safe", "thermite", "keypad", "wires", "lockpick", "fingerprint", "hotwire", "lasers", "keyfiling" or "tracker". The GTA drill replaces the progress bar, since it can't be finished faster than TOB.DrillTime. Without tobs_minigames, or if a GTA screen doesn't load, the normal minigame runs instead.

Per bank, in config/banks.lua:

B1 = {
    label = "Paleto Bay (Blaine County Savings)",
    minigames = {hack = "hack", gate = {type = "keypad", difficulty = "hard"}, drill = "drill"},
    ...

To add a language, copy the en block in locales/locales.lua, rename it, translate it and keep the %s and %d placeholders.

docs.text:
The banks live in config/banks.lua: Paleto (B1) and the six Fleeca banks (F1–F6). Turn one off with enabled = false, all Fleeca banks with TOB.FleecaBanks = false, and give any bank its own cash and cooldown.

Adding a bank

Copy a bank's block, rename it (for example B2) and fill in the positions. Stand on each spot in game and type /bankcoords: it prints your position and heading ready to paste.

Setting What it is doors.startloc The "Start bank heist" panel. animcoords is where the player stands gate The security gate: position, closed angle (h) and prompt position (txtloc) vault The vault door and its prompt position prop.first Where the used card is left trolley1–trolley3 The 3 trolley spawns, with angle (h) objects The same 3 spots, used for cleanup doors.secondloc The panel that opens the inner gate (leave it out for a bank without one) gateTrolleys The trolleys behind the inner gate. Default {"trolley1", "trolley2"} (Paleto: {"trolley2", "trolley3"}) vaultTurn Degrees the vault door turns to open: -90 by default, 90 for a door hung the other way (Paleto) label The bank's name in Discord logs minigames This bank's own hack, gate and drill minigame

Banks with other door models can set gateModel and vaultModel (a model name or a hash number).

docs.title: The heist
docs.text:
1. At least TOB.mincops police must be online (on QBCore and Qbox: on duty), and at least TOB.MinCrew robbers must be at the panel.
  2. A player with a Malicious Access Card uses Start bank heist at the bank's security panel (press E, or with ox_target).
  3. The card is used up and police are alerted. At Paleto, the bank alarm starts ringing.
  4. The robber opens a laptop at the panel and plays the hacking minigame: an ox_lib skill check, or GTA Online's hacking laptop when tobs_minigames is running (every bank by default). Failing it, or taking longer than TOB.CardTime, ends the heist.
  5. The hack runs for TOB.hacktime (1 minute by default).
  6. If a vault item is set, the robber has TOB.timer seconds to plant thermite on the vault door, which then burns through.
  7. The vault opens. The crew has TOB.timer (5 minutes) to loot the 3 trolleys, with a countdown at the bank. One trolley stands in front of the inner gate and can be looted straight away; the other two are behind it. Grabbing pays for the time spent, and X stops early. See Grabbing and the deposit boxes.
  8. To reach the two trolleys behind the gate, the robber opens it at its panel with the bank's gate minigame (thermite with tobs_minigames, otherwise the hacking minigame again). Failing it keeps the gate shut, so they can try again. A gold or diamond trolley, when there is one, is always behind the gate.
  9. When every trolley is empty or the time runs out, the vault closes after TOB.VaultCloseDelay seconds. The bank goes on cooldown (TOB.cooldown, 10 minutes). Everyone sees what they got, and the crew's total.

The heist also ends if the robber leaves the bank. If the robber disconnects, the nearest crew member at the bank takes over and leads the rest of the heist. Heists can also be blocked by the global rules, restart protection or an admin's heist switch; the player is always told why.

docs.title: For police
docs.text:
• Every officer gets an alert, and a flashing red blip marks the bank until the heist ends. Officers who go on duty during a heist get the blip too.
  • Officers can lock and unlock the security gate and the vault door.
  • Police can't start or loot the heist.
  • Using a dispatch script? See Dispatch.

docs.title: Anti-cheat
docs.text:
The server runs the whole heist: every step, every timer and every payout. Players' games only ask, so mod menus can't skip steps or fake payouts:

  • The vault only opens when the server says the hack (and the vault item) is done. Nobody can open it early.
  • Trolleys can only be looted while the vault is open, and the two behind the inner gate only after it's open.
  • Trolleys pay for the time actually spent grabbing, never more than the trolley holds, and only at the trolley.
  • Each trolley can be looted once per heist, and a player drills one deposit box at a time, for as long as drilling takes.
  • Only police can lock and unlock the doors. The robber's gate and vault are opened by the server.
  • Starting, looting and drilling check that the player is there. This needs OneSync; without it the console shows a warning.
  • A heist that somehow gets stuck ends automatically, and cooldowns survive restarts.

Blocked attempts can be posted to Discord.

Coming from tobs_blaine

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Check the server console and the F8 console first. Errors show tobs_bankrobbery.

Type /tobcheck first: the health check lists missing items, resources, permissions and settings in the server console. It also runs a few seconds after the server starts.

docs.title: Starting a heist
docs.text:
“Not enough police” but police are online
  • Qbox / QBCore: only officers who are on duty count. Clock in, or set TOB.PoliceOnDuty = false.
  • Your police job or group has a different name. Set TOB.PoliceJob in config/config.lua.
  • To test on your own, use /tobtest: it skips the police, crew and cooldown rules.
No “Start bank heist” prompt
  • Police can't start heists.
  • With ox_target running there's no floating text: target the panel. TOB.Target = "none" brings back press E.
  • The bank is on cooldown or already being robbed.
“You need 2 robbers at the panel (1 here)”

TOB.MinCrew is set above 1. More robbers need to stand within TOB.CrewRadius meters of the panel.

“Bank heists are paused”

An admin paused heists with /tobpause. /tobpause off allows them again, and so does a server restart.

“The city restarts soon”

A txAdmin restart is scheduled within SV.BlockBeforeRestart minutes. Set it to 0 to turn this off.

Fleeca heists clash with another script

Set TOB.FleecaBanks = false to keep only Paleto.

docs.title: Items, inventory and payouts
docs.text:
“You don't have a malicious access card” but I have one

The item must be named exactly id_card_f. See Installation.

“You need a drill to open the deposit boxes”

Add a drill item to your inventory, or set TOB.DrillItem = "" so no item is needed.

Items aren't found on QBCore

If ox_inventory is running, the items must be in ox_inventory/data/items.lua; otherwise in qb-core/shared/items.lua. See Installation.

“Your pockets are full”

The player's inventory can't take the loot items. They can make room and keep grabbing; a deposit box stays closed so it can be drilled again.

Payouts are too high or too low

Each trolley pays its bank's cash (in config/banks.lua; TOB.TrolleyCash for banks without one) when fully grabbed; a heist has 3 trolleys plus the deposit boxes. A gold or diamond trolley pays 44 items instead (itemCount in TOB.SpecialTrolleys). The end log in the console and on Discord shows what every player got, for example $199,363 ($100,123 cash, 44 × diamond): the total counts the items at their trolley's value.

A gold or diamond trolley pays cash, not gold bars or diamonds

The item isn't in your inventory yet, so the script pays cash rather than nothing. Add goldbar / diamond from the install/ folder and restart your inventory (ox_inventory only reads its items when it starts).

“Open the inner gate to reach the trolleys behind it.”

Two trolleys are behind the inner gate. Open it at its panel first. If a trolley in front of the gate says this, its gateTrolleys in config/banks.lua don't match your vault.

docs.title: Minigames, prompts and notifications
docs.text:
The minigame doesn't appear

The default minigame needs ox_lib. Put ensure ox_lib above ensure tobs_bankrobbery, use another minigame, or turn it off with TOB.HackMinigame = "none".

The ox_lib skill check shows instead of GTA's laptop, the drill or thermite

Those games come from tobs_minigames. Start it above tobs_bankrobbery in server.cfg. Without it, or if a GTA screen doesn't load, the normal minigame runs on purpose.

Error about progressBars

Without ox_lib the script uses progressBars. Install either one.

No notifications

Set TOB.Notify to what you run, for example "ox_lib", or "native" for GTA notifications.

docs.title: Admin commands and logs
docs.text:
No permission for /tobreset, /tobpause, /tobtest or /tobcheck

Add the add_ace lines from Installation to server.cfg, or run the command in the server console (not /tobtest: it's for players in game).

Discord logs don't arrive

Check SV.Webhook in config/config_server.lua is the full URL and the webhook still exists. The logs are also printed in the server console.

“Bank … is missing … and was skipped” in the console

A bank in TOB.Banks is missing a setting (for example after a copy-paste). The console names the bank and the missing settings. The other banks keep working.

docs.title: Server setup
docs.text:
“No framework found” in the console

tobs_bankrobbery started before your framework. Move ensure tobs_bankrobbery below ensure qbx_core, es_extended or qb-core, or set TOB.Framework in config/config.lua.

Error: attempt to index a nil value (global 'Bridge')

No framework was found when the script started. See “No framework found” above.

“OneSync is off” in the console

Add set onesync on to server.cfg. Without OneSync the server can't see where players are, so the anti-cheat can't check that players are at the bank.

Police don't see the GPS tracker

TOB.Tracker needs OneSync (the server sends the robber's position). The console warns at startup when it's off.

docs.title: Models and animations
docs.text:
Gold or diamond trolleys look like cash trolleys

Their models are from game build 2060. Set sv_enforceGameBuild 2060 (or newer) in server.cfg; they still pay their gold bars or diamonds either way.

The vault door opens the wrong way (into the wall or the vault)

Set vaultTurn on that bank in config/banks.lua: -90 (the default) or 90 for a door hung the other way, like Paleto's.

The vault room or doors look wrong

Check that stream/v_int_41.ytyp is inside the tobs_bankrobbery folder.

The laptop or thermite animation looks off

Animations are placed from the bank's positions in the config, so a custom bank may need tuned positions. Turn them off with TOB.LaptopHack = false or TOB.VaultItemAnim = "weld", and please report it on GitHub.

Still stuck? Open an issue on GitHub with your framework, version and the error.

docs.title: tobs_burnerphones
docs.text:
v1.0.0 Qbox 2 languages Cfx escrow

Throwaway flip phones for criminals. Every SIM card has its own number and a few uses before it burns out. Text, call, swap SIMs and snap them when it gets hot, while police trace and terminate the numbers they find.

Buy · $15 Installation

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Framework Qbox Requires qbx_core, ox_lib, ox_inventory, ox_target, oxmysql, pma-voice Phone resource None needed: it brings its own flip phone (no NPWD, no qb-phone) Police A built-in police menu (/burner and police computers), or tobs_policemdt / any MDT through exports Languages English, Danish Licence Paid, delivered through Cfx asset escrow. config.lua, the texts and the item / SQL files are open: What you can edit

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Phones and SIM cards

    The handset and the SIM are separate items. Swap, trade or snap SIMs; the phone itself survives.

    How it works

  • Limited uses

    Each SIM rolls 10–20 uses. A text costs 1, a call 2 once it's answered. At 0 the SIM burns out.

    Uses

  • Police tracing

    Officers look up a number, read its messages and calls, and terminate it: "SIGNAL TERMINATED".

    Police

  • Built for privacy

    Numbers, messages and calls are stored without the character's ID, and wiped when a SIM dies.

    Privacy

docs.text: Questions or a bug? Ask on Discord: support for the script is free. Please say your Qbox version and what the F8 and server consoles show.

docs.title: 1.0.0 · 2026-10-10
docs.text:
The first release.

  • Burner flip phones with their own screen: texts, calls through pma-voice, contacts. No phone resource needed
  • Separate SIM cards with a 10-digit number and 10–20 uses: insert, eject, trade or snap them
  • Dealers at Vespucci, Grove Street and Mirror Park, unmarked by default
  • Police: a built-in menu (/burner and police computers) to look up a number, read its history and terminate it; exports for tobs_policemdt and other MDTs. On-duty officers only, one termination per 5 seconds
  • Privacy: nothing stored with the character's ID; messages and calls wiped when a SIM dies
  • Admin tools: /giveburner, /killburner, /burnerterminal, Discord logs
  • Languages: English and Danish

tobs_burnerphones is protected by Cfx asset escrow: most of its code is encrypted, so it only runs on servers the buyer owns. The files you need to set it up stay open:

docs.title: Changing what the script does
docs.text:
• Settings first: almost everything is a setting in config.lua. If something you need is missing, ask on Discord: it may become a setting.
  • From your own scripts: give out burners, look numbers up, read their history and terminate them with the exports.
  • Don't edit encrypted files. Changing or renaming them stops the script from starting. Download a fresh copy from the portal if it happened.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text: All exports are server-side.

docs.title: Give a burner
docs.text:
local ok, number = exports.tobs_burnerphones:createBurner(source)

Gives the player a working phone with a new SIM in it. number is the new 10-digit number.

docs.title: For MDTs
docs.text: These three only work for the resources in Config.Blacklist.mdtResource (see Police). Anything else gets NOT_ALLOWED_RESOURCE.

docs.title: Look up a number
docs.text:
local info = exports.tobs_burnerphones:lookupNumber('3576713931')

Returns nil for an unknown or invalid number, otherwise:

{
    number = '3576713931',
    formatted = '357-671-3931',
    status = 'active',
    usesLeft = 12,
    maxUses = 17,
    blacklisted = false,
}

docs.title: Read a number's history
docs.text:
local history, err = exports.tobs_burnerphones:readHistory(officerSrc, number)

Checks the officer (job, grade, on duty) and logs the read. Returns nil, err when refused, otherwise:

{
    number = '3576713931',
    formatted = '357-671-3931',
    blacklisted = false,
    messages = {
        { outbound = true, partner = '541-220-8873', body = 'Meet at the docks', createdAt = ... },
    },
    calls = {
        { outbound = false, partner = '541-220-8873', duration = 42, reason = 'completed', startedAt = ... },
    },
}

status is 'active' or 'blacklisted'; a call's reason is completed, rejected, missed, blacklisted, depleted or dropped.

There's no sender name: burners don't store who used them.

docs.title: Terminate a number
docs.text:
local ok, err = exports.tobs_burnerphones:blacklistNumber(officerSrc, number, reason)

Checks the officer (job, grade, on duty, cooldown), terminates the number and logs it.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: Code Meaning NOT_ALLOWED_RESOURCE Your resource isn't in mdtResource NO_PERMISSION Wrong job, too low a grade, or off duty RATE_LIMITED The officer terminated a number less than cooldownMs ago INVALID_NUMBER Not a 10-digit burner number NOT_FOUND No burner has that number ALREADY_BLACKLISTED Already terminated

docs.title: Handsets and SIM cards
docs.text:
The phone and the number are separate items, so players can swap, trade and replace SIM cards:

Item What it is burner_phone The handset. It has no number of its own and is useless without a SIM. burner_sim The SIM card: the phone number, a serial and the uses left on it. burner_fried A burnt SIM, given back when a number dies (Config.ConvertOnDeath). Evidence, nothing more.
  • Insert a SIM: use a SIM while carrying an empty handset.
  • Eject the SIM (in the phone's menu): take it out without destroying it, to move it to another handset or hand it to someone.
  • Snap the SIM: destroy it on the spot. Its stored messages and calls are wiped.
  • Open the phone: use it from the inventory. F3 closes it (players can change the key in GTA's keybind settings).

When a number dies, the handset survives: it's blanked and takes a new SIM. Players lose the number, not the phone they paid for.

docs.title: Getting a burner
docs.text:
• Dealers: three unmarked dealers sell handsets ($450) and SIM cards ($900) for cash, at Vespucci beach, Grove Street and Mirror Park. They have no map blip by default: a burner dealer you can find on the map isn't much of a burner dealer. Prices, limits, locations and the blip are in Config.Dealers.
  • Admins: /giveburner [player id] gives a complete, working burner.
  • Your scripts: exports.tobs_burnerphones:createBurner(source), for a shop, a job reward or a loot table. See For developers.

docs.title: The phone
docs.text:
A flip phone with its own screen, worked with the mouse or the keyboard:

  • Messages: threads per number, up to 255 characters a text.
  • Dialer: calls go through pma-voice and end on their own after 15 minutes.
  • Contacts: saved in the player's own game, never in the database.

Keypad tones, the ringtone and the message alert are made by the phone itself, so there are no sound files to install.

Key Home screen Dialer Text editor 1 2 3 Messages / Dialer / Contacts Types the digit Types text 0–9 Navigation Types the digit Types text Enter — Places the call Sends the message Esc Closes the phone Clears / back Back

docs.title: Uses
docs.text:
Each new SIM rolls a number of uses (10–20 by default). What each action costs:

Action Cost Text 1 use Call 2 uses, only once the other side answers Contacts, menus, opening the phone Free

At 3 uses left the screen shows a low-signal warning. At 0 the SIM burns out: the number is terminated and the player gets a burner_fried back. All in Config.Uses and Config.UseCost.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Numbers have 10 digits, shown as 357-671-3931, and start with 35, 54 or 73 by default (Config.Number). Every number is unique, and a terminated number never comes back.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
Burners aren't tied to the character using them:

  • Numbers, messages and calls are stored without the character's citizen ID.
  • Contacts stay in the player's own game.
  • Snapping a SIM wipes its messages and calls; terminating a number wipes them too (Config.Blacklist.purgeLogs).
  • Old messages and calls are cleared after 30 days (Config.Limits.messageHistoryDays).
  • Staff logs (Config.Logging) can still show which player did what, so abuse can be looked into. identify = false turns that off.

So police can prove a number sent a message, not who sent it: that's up to the investigation.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Qbox (qbx_core)
  • ox_lib, ox_inventory, ox_target and oxmysql
  • pma-voice for the calls
  • A server build from the last few months (escrowed resources need a recent one)

docs.title: Get the script
docs.text:
1. Buy tobs_burnerphones in the store. Tebex asks you to log in with your Cfx.re account: use the account your server's licence key belongs to.

  2. Log in at portal.cfx.re, open Assets → Granted Assets and download tobs_burnerphones.

Same Cfx.re account as the licence key

Escrowed scripts only start on servers whose licence key belongs to the account that bought them. Bought it on another account? See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Unzip it and put the tobs_burnerphones folder in your server's resources folder. Don't rename the folder.

  2. Import sql/install.sql into your database. It makes four tables: tobs_burner_numbers, tobs_burner_messages, tobs_burner_calls and tobs_burner_blacklist.

  3. Copy the three items from items.txt into [ox]/ox_inventory/data/items.lua:

    ['burner_phone'] = {
    label = 'Burner Phone',
    weight = 180,
    stack = false,
    close = true,
    consume = 0,
    description = 'A cheap prepaid handset. Useless without a SIM card.',
    client = { export = 'tobs_burnerphones.useBurner' }
},

['burner_sim'] = {
    label = 'Burner SIM',
    weight = 5,
    stack = false,
    close = true,
    consume = 0,
    description = 'A prepaid SIM card. Holds the number and whatever uses are left on it.',
    client = { export = 'tobs_burnerphones.useSim' }
},

['burner_fried'] = {
    label = 'Burnt SIM',
    weight = 5,
    stack = true,
    close = true,
    consume = 0,
    description = 'A dead SIM card. The number on it is gone for good.'
},

  4. Copy the item images from the script's images/ folder (burner_phone.png, burner_sim.png, burner_fried.png) into [ox]/ox_inventory/web/images/.

  5. Add it to server.cfg, below Qbox and the ox resources:

    ensure tobs_burnerphones

  6. Optional: Danish texts. The language follows ox_lib's setting:

    setr ox:locale da

  7. Restart the server.

The default settings work as they are. Everything you can change is on the Configuration page.

docs.title: Test it in game
docs.text:
1. As an admin, type /giveburner [your id]: you get a working phone with a SIM in it.
  2. Use the phone from your inventory to open it; F3 closes it.
  3. Give a second phone to another player (or a second game) and text or call between them.
  4. As an on-duty police officer (grade 2 or higher by default), type /burner and look the number up. Or use the police computer at Mission Row.

docs.title: Police computers
docs.text: Officers can also open the police menu at a computer in the station. One is set up at Mission Row as an example. If your police station uses another MLO, the computer is in a different spot: stand at the computer as an admin, type /burnerterminal, and paste the line it copies into Config.Police.terminals in config.lua (replace the example, or add more). Restart the script. More on the Police page.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
1. Download the new version from portal.cfx.re (Granted Assets). Every update is free.
  2. Keep a copy of your config.lua and any texts you changed in locales/.
  3. Replace the tobs_burnerphones folder, then put your settings back into the new config.lua (new versions may add settings).
  4. Run any new SQL the changelog mentions, then restart the server.

docs.title: Police
docs.text:
Police can trace burners with or without an MDT. Once officers have a number (a seized phone, a witness, a text on another phone), they can:

  • Look it up: is it active or terminated, and how many uses are left.
  • Read its history: the messages and calls stored for it. Read it before terminating: a terminated number's history is wiped when purgeLogs is on.
  • Terminate it: the holder's phone shows SIGNAL TERMINATED, the SIM burns out, and the number can never be used again.

docs.title: Who can do it
docs.text:
The same rules apply to the menu, the MDTs and the exports (Config.Blacklist):

Setting Default What it does allowedJobs police, sheriff Jobs that may use it minGrade 2 Lowest job grade requireOnDuty true Officers must be on duty cooldownMs 5000 One termination per officer every 5 seconds

Every termination and every history read is logged (Config.Logging).

docs.title: The police menu
docs.text:
Built in, no MDT needed (Config.Police):

  • /burner opens it anywhere. Set command = false to allow it only at police computers (the server then checks the officer is standing at one).

  • Police computers open it with ox_target. One is set up at Mission Row as an example. Positions depend on your police station's MLO, so if yours is different, move it: stand at the computer as an admin, type /burnerterminal and paste the line it copies into terminals (add more lines for more computers):

    terminals = {
    { coords = vec3(450.19, -979.25, 30.69), radius = 0.6, label = 'Police computer' },
},

  • enabled = false turns the menu off, for servers that do it all in their MDT.

docs.title: With tobs_policemdt or another MDT
docs.text:
tobs_policemdt has burner lookups, history and termination built in. Other MDTs can use the same exports.

Config.Blacklist.mdtResource decides which resources may call them:

mdtResource = 'tobs_policemdt',                -- only tobs_policemdt
mdtResource = { 'tobs_policemdt', 'ps-mdt' },  -- several
mdtResource = false,                           -- any resource

clientEvent = true also lets an MDT terminate a number from the officer's game with the tobs_burnerphones:server:blacklistNumber event. Leave it false (the default) unless your MDT needs it: tobs_policemdt uses the exports.

docs.title: Admins
docs.text: /killburner [number] [reason] terminates a number by hand, without the police rules.

docs.title: "You lack the required entitlement"
docs.text:
The server's licence key belongs to another Cfx.re account than the one that bought the script.

  • Check which account the key is on at portal.cfx.re (Server Keys).
  • The script must be under Granted Assets on that same account. If you bought it on another account, contact us through the store with your order ID.
  • Restart the server after changing the key.

docs.title: The script doesn't start after editing it
docs.text: The encrypted files (client/, server/, shared/) and the folder name can't be changed. Download a fresh copy from the portal and only edit the open files.

docs.title: "Failed to load" or a script error right at start
docs.text: Update your server artifacts: escrowed resources need a recent build.

docs.title: The phone or SIM does nothing when used
docs.text:
• The items are missing their client = { export = ... } line: copy them again from items.txt (Installation, step 3).
  • ensure tobs_burnerphones must come after ox_inventory in server.cfg.

docs.title: Items have no picture
docs.text: Copy the three PNGs from images/ into [ox]/ox_inventory/web/images/ and restart ox_inventory.

docs.title: "Insert a SIM" / the phone won't open
docs.text: A handset needs a SIM: use a burner_sim while carrying an empty phone.

docs.title: Calls connect but nobody can hear each other
docs.text: Calls use pma-voice. Check that it's running and that both players can use normal voice chat.

docs.title: A text or call is refused
docs.text:
• The SIM has too few uses left for it (Config.RejectIfInsufficientUses).
  • The other number is terminated or doesn't exist.

docs.title: /burner says no permission
docs.text: The officer needs a job in allowedJobs, a grade of at least minGrade (2 by default) and to be on duty.

docs.title: The MDT gets NOT_ALLOWED_RESOURCE
docs.text: Add your MDT's resource name to Config.Blacklist.mdtResource, or set it to false.

docs.title: History is empty
docs.text: The number was terminated or snapped and purgeLogs is on, or the messages were older than 30 days. Read the history before terminating a number.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Ask on Discord with your Qbox version, what you did, and what the F8 and server consoles show.

docs.text: Updates are free: download the new version from portal.cfx.re (Granted Assets) and follow Updating.

docs.title: 1.0.0 · 2026-10-10
docs.text:
The first release.

  • Drop-in replacement for the default chat: every script written for chat keeps working
  • Channels: /me and /do with speech bubbles, /ooc, police and EMS radio with ranks, and a staff channel. Each with its own range, job, duty, colour and cooldown, and its own tab for radios
  • Moderation: mutes that survive a reconnect, /clearall, /slowmode, /chatlock, /chatspy, word and spam filters, /announce, Discord logs
  • For players: grouped messages, emojis and @mentions, chat history for joiners, a new-messages pill, and a settings menu with five themes, six accent colours, size, width and position
  • Exports: sendToChannel, announce, notify, isMuted, mute, unmute
  • Languages: English and Danish

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Every channel in Config.Channels gets its own command, colour, icon and label. These are included:

Command Channel Who and where /me, /do Actions Players within 20 m, with a speech bubble above your head and your character name /ooc Out of character Players within 20 m, with your FiveM name /pd Police radio Police on duty only, with its own tab. Shows the officer's rank: LSPD │ SERGEANT Sofie Rask /ems EMS radio EMS on duty only, with its own tab /staff Staff chat Staff only (the tobs_chat.staff ace), with its own tab

Bleeter, ads and dark chat aren't part of it: they belong in the phone (lb-phone, NPWD and the like).

docs.title: A line without a command
docs.text:
A line typed without a command goes to everyone on the server, like in the default chat. Config.PlainChat can change that:

Value What a plain line does 'global' (default) Goes to everyone on the server 'ooc' Goes into /ooc: only the players around you 'off' Isn't sent; the player is told to start with a command

docs.title: Ranks
docs.text: With rank = true, the sender's rank goes before their name. It's the job's grade name, from qbx_core/shared/jobs.lua (Recruit, Officer, Sergeant, ...). After a setjob or a promotion, the new rank shows within 2 seconds. It's on for /pd by default.

docs.title: Turning a channel off
docs.text:
Every channel has enabled = true or false. A channel that's off has no command, so a framework's own version (qbx_core's /me or /ooc) works instead.

Your MDT has its own police chat?

Set the pd channel to enabled = false, so officers don't have two police chats.

docs.title: Adding or changing a channel
docs.text:
Each channel is one line in Config.Channels. For example, a mechanic radio:

{ enabled = true, command = 'mech', label = 'MECHANIC', icon = 'radio', color = '#f2b84b',
  jobs = { mechanic = 0 }, onDuty = true, name = 'character', rank = true, mode = true, cooldown = 500 },
Option What it does enabled true = on, false = off command The /command (without /); also the channel's id label Shown before the name, and on its tab icon chat, me, do, megaphone, shield, cross, radio, star or info color The card's colour (#rrggbb) range Metres around the sender; leave it out for everyone on the server (same routing bucket either way) jobs { jobname = minimum grade, ... }; leave it out for any job onDuty true = the job must be on duty (needs jobs) ace An ace the sender needs, e.g. Config.StaffAce name 'character' (first and last name) or 'player' (FiveM name) rank true = the rank before the name (needs jobs) bubble Also show a bubble above the sender's head (needs a range) italic The text in italics, for actions cooldown ms between two messages from the same player in this channel mode true = a tab in the chat box, for chats people stay in, like a radio

A broken channel is reported in the console at startup and left out. So is a job channel on a server without a framework.

docs.title: Checked on the server
docs.text: Everything is checked on the server when a message is sent: the job and duty, the range and routing bucket, the cooldown, mutes, and the word and spam filters. Going off duty stops the radio reaching you within 2 seconds.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Everything is in config.lua, one of the files you can edit. Every setting is also explained in the file. Restart the script after a change.

docs.title: General
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Config.Framework 'auto' 'auto', 'qbox' or 'none'. With 'none', job channels are off; everything else works Config.StaffAce 'tobs_chat.staff' The ace that makes a player staff (moderation commands and the staff channel) Config.MaxLength 256 Longest message a player can send, in characters Config.Cooldown 750 Minimum ms between two chat messages from the same player. Commands aren't limited by it Config.AllowColorCodes true Lets players colour their messages with ^1–^9. false strips them (script messages keep their colours) Config.PlainChat 'global' Where a line without a command goes: 'global', 'ooc' or 'off' (Channels) Config.MaxMessages 100 Messages kept in the chat window Config.HistorySize 30 Sent messages a player can bring back with ↑ Config.JoinMessages / QuitMessages true "X joined" and "X left" lines. Skipped while qbx_chat_theme runs, because it sends its own

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Config.OpenKey 'T' Opens the chat Config.MenuKey '' Opens the settings menu. '' = no key by default: players bind it themselves. The gear and /chatsettings always work Config.ToggleKey 'L' Cycles when the chat shows. false = no key (/toggleChat still works)

Players can rebind the keys in the GTA key settings. Changing these only affects players who never pressed them before: that's how FiveM key mappings work.

docs.title: Chat history for joiners
docs.text:
Config.ChatHistory

Setting Default What it does enabled true Show recent public chat to players who join or reconnect size 40 Messages kept maxAgeMinutes 30 Older ones aren't shown

Only normal chat to everyone is kept: never channels, radios, or anything a script sends.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text: Config.Channels: every option, with an example, is on the Channels page.

docs.title: Speech bubbles
docs.text:
Config.Bubbles

Setting Default What it does duration 7000 ms on screen height 0.45 Metres above the head

docs.title: Emojis and mentions
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Config.Emojis true :smile:-style codes and the emoji picker Config.Mentions.enabled true @name or @id highlights the message for that player, with a sound Config.Mentions.max 5 Most players one message can ping

docs.title: Word and spam filters
docs.text:
Config.WordFilter

Setting Default What it does enabled true Turns the filter on action 'censor' 'censor' replaces the word with ****, 'block' drops the whole message words { 'badword', 'anotherbadword' } Whole words, not case sensitive: add your own

Config.Spam (staff are exempt)

Setting Default What it does enabled true Turns the spam filter on repeatSeconds 30 The same message again within this time is refused repeatIgnore { 'me', 'do' } Channels never checked for repeats caps { enabled = true, minLetters = 12, ratio = 0.7, action = 'lower' } Messages with at least 12 letters, 70 % of them capitals, are lowercased ('lower') or refused ('block')

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Config.Logs. The Discord webhook isn't in this file, because it's a secret: set it in server.cfg (Moderation).

Setting Default What it does console true Print every player message in the server console discord true Send to the webhook (does nothing until it's set) batchSeconds 5 Collect messages and post them together, so Discord doesn't rate-limit chat / channels / moderation true Which kinds of messages are logged

docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Config.Themes all five The themes players can choose from, in this order: 'frosted', 'midnight', 'compact', 'daylight', 'tinted'. With one left, the theme choice disappears

Config.Defaults: what new players start with. Every player can change these in their settings menu.

Setting Default Choices theme 'frosted' One of Config.Themes accent 'default' 'default' (ice blue), or '#e6b85c' (gold), '#4fd1a5' (mint), '#a29bfe' (violet), '#ff7a93' (rose), '#e9eaee' (white) size 100 Text size in %: 90, 100, 115 or 130 background 'medium' 'light', 'medium' or 'dark' width 'normal' 'narrow', 'normal' or 'wide' position 'top' 'top', 'middle' or 'bottom' (just above the minimap) timestamps false The time on every message visibility 'auto' 'auto' (shows on new messages), 'always' or 'hidden' (only while typing) fadeSeconds 10 For 'auto': seconds a new message stays: 5, 10, 20 or 30 bubbles true Speech bubbles above other players' heads mentionSound true A sound when someone @mentions you

docs.title: What you can edit
docs.text:
tobs_chat is protected by Cfx asset escrow: its Lua code is encrypted, so it only runs on servers the buyer owns. The files you need to set it up and style it stay open:

File What's in it config.lua Every setting: channels, keys, limits, filters, logs, themes and the defaults for new players. See Configuration locales/en.json, locales/da.json Every text players and staff see. Change them, or add a language (copy en.json to xx.json and set setr ox:locale xx) server/bridge.lua Where jobs, grades, duty and character names come from. Change it if your framework is edited or custom web/ The chat page itself: style.css (colours and themes, as tokens at the top of the file), app.js, format.js, the font and the theme pictures

Everything else in client/, server/ and shared/ is encrypted.

docs.title: Changing what the script does
docs.text:
• Settings first: almost everything is a setting in config.lua. If something you need is missing, ask on Discord: it may become a setting.
  • From your own scripts: post in channels, make announcements, send notices and mute players with the exports. Every script written for the default chat works as it is.
  • Restyling: the colours, corners and shadows of each theme are tokens at the top and bottom of web/style.css. Keep a copy of your changes: an update replaces the file.
  • Don't edit encrypted files. Changing or renaming them stops the script from starting. Download a fresh copy from the portal if it happened.

docs.title: The default chat's API
docs.text:
tobs_chat answers everything the default chat resource does, so existing scripts work unchanged:

  • chat:addMessage, chat:addSuggestion, chat:addSuggestions, chat:removeSuggestion, chatMessage
  • exports.chat:addMessage, registerMessageHook, registerMode
  • chat:addTemplate and /toggleChat

The resource provides chat, so resources that depend on chat start, and exports.chat:* reaches tobs_chat.

docs.title: Message styles
docs.text:
tobs_chat has a few message styles of its own, picked with templateId:

-- client
TriggerEvent('chat:addMessage', { templateId = 'success', args = { 'Garage', 'Vehicle stored' } })

-- server
TriggerClientEvent('chat:addMessage', source, { templateId = 'error', args = { 'Bank', 'Not enough money' } })
templateId Shows default Name {0} above the text {1}, or just {0} with one arg; a chat icon in the accent colour success, error, warning, info The same card with a green tick, red alert, amber shield or blue info icon announce The full-width announcement card: title {0}, text {1} join, quit, print A small grey server line with an enter, leave or console icon

docs.title: Exports
docs.text:
All of them run on the server, check their arguments, return false when something is wrong, and log which resource called them.

-- post in a channel: dispatch into the police radio, a robbery alarm into /me range, ...
-- the channel's jobs and ace decide who gets it; coords (and bucket) are used for range channels
exports.tobs_chat:sendToChannel('pd', { text = '10-90 at Fleeca Legion', author = 'Dispatch' })
exports.tobs_chat:sendToChannel('me', { text = 'a car alarm goes off', coords = vector3(x, y, z), bucket = 0 })

-- an announcement card for everyone; the title is optional
exports.tobs_chat:announce('Server restart in 10 minutes', 'Server')

-- a notice card for one player: 'success', 'error', 'warning' or 'info'
exports.tobs_chat:notify(source, 'success', 'Vehicle stored', 'Garage')

-- mutes, e.g. from an anticheat
local muted, secondsLeft = exports.tobs_chat:isMuted(source)
exports.tobs_chat:mute(source, 10, 'spam')   -- minutes, reason
exports.tobs_chat:unmute(source)

docs.title: Message details
docs.text:
• Sender ID: messages players type carry their server ID (playerId), shown next to the name. A message hook can remove it with updateMessage({ playerId = false }).
  • Colour: a message's color colours the card's icon. Colours too dark to read on the dark cards are lightened automatically.
  • Colour codes: ^0–^9, ^* (bold), ^_ (underline), ^~ (strikethrough) and ^r (reset) work in every message.
  • Templates: chat:addTemplate(id, html) adds or replaces a template.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: icon: material/star-outline description: What tobs_chat does for players: the chat box, tabs, grouping, bubbles, emojis, mentions, history, the settings menu and the five themes.

docs.title: The chat box
docs.text:
• T opens the chat. Enter sends, Esc closes.
  • Start with / for commands. Suggestions show as you type, with the parameter you're on highlighted. The suggestion with the TAB key on it is the one Tab completes.
  • ↑ / ↓ brings back what you sent before. Page Up / Page Down scrolls. If new messages arrive while you're scrolled up, a "2 new ↓" pill takes you back down.
  • L (or /toggleChat) switches between showing the chat on new messages, always, or only while typing.
  • /clear empties your own chat.

Every card shows the sender's server ID next to the name, so players can report someone without asking for their ID.

docs.title: Channel tabs
docs.text:
Above the chat: All, plus a tab for each radio or staff chat the player can use, each with its channel's colour. A tab shows only that channel, and what you type goes there. Tab on an empty message switches tabs, and a dot marks a tab with messages you haven't seen.

A civilian sees no tabs at all: only players with a radio or the staff channel get them.

docs.title: Grouped messages
docs.text: Several messages in a row from the same player in the same channel, within a minute, share one card (up to six lines). Busy chats take up less of the screen.

docs.title: Speech bubbles
docs.text:
/me and /do also show the text in a bubble above the player's head. The bubble follows the head while they walk, hides behind walls, and is gone after 7 seconds. Every player can turn bubbles off for themselves.

A `/me` bubble, with its tail pointing down at the player.

docs.title: Emojis and mentions
docs.text:
• The smiley in the chat box opens an emoji picker; :fire:-style codes work too.
  • @name or @id pings that player with a highlighted card and a soft sound. Typing @ lists the players around you, and Tab or a click puts in their ID. Every player can mute the sound.

docs.title: Chat history for joiners
docs.text: Joining or reconnecting shows the last public chat (up to 40 messages from the last 30 minutes, dimmed), so players know what was just said. Channels and radios are never in it.

docs.title: Settings menu
docs.text:
Every player has their own settings menu, saved on their computer. It opens with the gear in the chat box, /chatsettings, or a key they bind themselves ("Open chat settings" in the GTA key settings). New players get a one-time tip about it. The menu sits next to the chat, so every change shows straight away.

The Look tab: every change shows on the chat beside it. On the left, the channel tabs and a radio card with the officer's rank. Tab Settings Theme A picture of every theme; one click switches Look Accent colour (ice, gold, mint, violet, rose or white), text size 90–130 %, card background (light, medium or dark), width, and position (top left, middle left, or just above the minimap) Behaviour When the chat shows, how long new messages stay, timestamps, speech bubbles on or off, and the mention sound

On "new messages", each card fades out on its own. A card that mentions you stays twice as long, and an announcement three times as long.

Server owners set the defaults for new players in Config.Defaults, and which themes players can pick in Config.Themes (Configuration).

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
Each theme changes the whole look (cards, bubbles, input and settings), not only the colour. The accent colour works with every theme.

**Frosted** (default): frosted glass cards with a speech-bubble corner folded in the channel's colour.

**Midnight**: near-black square cards, a hairline of colour on top, letter-spaced names.

**Compact**: one line per message, so about twice as many fit. For busy servers.

**Daylight**: light cards with dark text, for bright daytime scenes.

**Tinted**: the whole card in its channel's colour, with solid round icons and filled labels.

docs.title: Safer than the default chat
docs.text:
Every chat line a player sends is checked on the server before anyone sees it: it must be one line, at most Config.MaxLength characters, and a player can send at most one message per Config.Cooldown ms. Anything else is dropped.

Names come from the server, never from the player. Player text is escaped before it's shown, so nobody can put HTML or scripts into other players' chat. /say is for the console and admins only (command.say).

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Measured with resmon on a Qbox server:

Idle, also with the chat open 0.00 ms When a message arrives 0.01 ms While using the settings menu 0.04–0.06 ms Memory about 410 KiB

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Qbox (qbx_core) for the job radios, ranks and character names. Without a framework everything else still works
  • ox_lib
  • A server build from the last few months (escrowed resources need a recent one)

No database, no items and no SQL.

docs.title: Get the script
docs.text:
1. Buy tobs_chat in the store. Tebex asks you to log in with your Cfx.re account: use the account your server's licence key belongs to.

  2. Log in at portal.cfx.re, open Assets → Granted Assets and download tobs_chat.

Same Cfx.re account as the licence key

Escrowed scripts only start on servers whose licence key belongs to the account that bought them. Bought it on another account? See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Unzip it and put the tobs_chat folder in your server's resources folder. Don't rename the folder.

  2. In server.cfg, replace the default chat with tobs_chat, in the same place (before your framework):

    # ensure chat
ensure tobs_chat

    Both handle the same events, so running them together shows every message twice. tobs_chat prints an error at startup if the default chat is still running.

  3. Give your staff the staff ace, so they can use the staff channel and the moderation commands:

    add_ace group.admin tobs_chat.staff allow

  4. Optional: Discord logs. Use set, not setr, so players can't read the webhook:

    set tobs_chat:webhook "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/..."

  5. Optional: Danish texts. The language follows ox_lib's setting:

    setr ox:locale da

  6. Restart the whole server, not only the resource, so the default chat isn't running any more.

The default settings work as they are. Everything you can change is on the Configuration page.

docs.title: qbx_chat_theme
docs.text: On Qbox you can remove qbx_chat_theme: it only styles the default chat. If you keep it, its join and quit lines are shown and tobs_chat's own are skipped.

docs.title: /me and /ooc from qbx_core
docs.text: qbx_core has its own /me (3D text) and /ooc. Players should only ever have one of each: in the chat box, /me, /ooc and the other channel commands always go to tobs_chat, whichever resource registered them last, and give a card and a speech bubble. To keep qbx_core's version instead, set that channel to enabled = false in config.lua.

docs.title: Test it in game
docs.text:
1. Press T, type hi and press Enter: a card with your name and ID.
  2. Type /me waves: an action card, and a bubble above your head.
  3. As a police officer on duty, type /pd test: a radio card with your rank, and an LSPD tab above the chat.
  4. Click the gear in the chat box (or type /chatsettings) and switch themes.
  5. As staff, type /announce Hello: a full-width announcement card for everyone.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
1. Download the new version from portal.cfx.re (Granted Assets). Every update is free.
  2. Keep a copy of your config.lua and any texts you changed in locales/.
  3. Replace the tobs_chat folder, then put your settings back into the new config.lua (new versions may add settings).
  4. Restart the server.

Players' own settings (theme, colours, position) are saved on their computer and stay after an update.

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text:
Only players with the staff ace (tobs_chat.staff by default) and the server console can use these. Players don't see them in the suggestions.

add_ace group.admin tobs_chat.staff allow

docs.title: Staff commands
docs.text:
Command What it does /announce message An announcement card for everyone on the server: full width, in the accent colour, and it stays on screen three times as long /chatmute id minutes reason Mutes a player in the chat and every channel. Stored by licence, so leaving and rejoining or a restart doesn't lift it /chatunmute id Lifts the mute /clearall Clears the chat for everyone, and the history new players see /slowmode seconds One public message per X seconds for players; /slowmode 0 turns it off /chatlock Closes the public chat and public channels for players. Job radios and the staff channel keep working. Run it again to open the chat /chatspy Shows you every channel message, whatever the range, job or routing bucket. Run it again to stop. Logged

Staff aren't held back by slow mode, the lock or the spam filter.

docs.title: Word filter
docs.text:
Config.WordFilter stars out the words in the list ('censor') or blocks the whole message ('block'). Whole words, not case sensitive.

Config.WordFilter = {
    enabled = true,
    action = 'censor',
    words = { 'badword', 'anotherbadword' },
}

docs.title: Spam filter
docs.text:
Config.Spam:

  • Repeats: the same message again within 30 seconds is refused ("You just sent that"). /me and /do are never checked, because repeating an action is normal roleplay.
  • Caps: long all-caps messages are turned into lowercase ('lower') or refused ('block').

docs.title: Discord logs
docs.text:
Set the webhook in server.cfg with set (not setr, so players can't read it):

set tobs_chat:webhook "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/..."

Logs go to the server console and, with the webhook set, to Discord in batches every 5 seconds: chat, channels, moderation and announcements. Config.Logs turns each part on or off. Nobody can ping @everyone through the logs.

docs.title: "You lack the required entitlement"
docs.text:
The server's licence key belongs to another Cfx.re account than the one that bought the script.

  • Check which account the key is on at portal.cfx.re (Server Keys).
  • The script must be under Granted Assets on that same account. If you bought it on another account, contact us through the store with your order ID.
  • Restart the server after changing the key.

docs.title: The script doesn't start after editing it
docs.text: The encrypted files (everything in client/, server/ and shared/ except server/bridge.lua) and the folder name can't be changed. Download a fresh copy from the portal and only edit the open files.

docs.title: "Failed to load" or a script error right at start
docs.text: Update your server artifacts: escrowed resources need a recent build.

docs.title: Every message shows twice
docs.text: The default chat is still running. Remove ensure chat from server.cfg (and from any .cfg it includes), then restart the whole server. tobs_chat prints "The default chat resource is running as well" at startup while both run.

docs.title: /me still shows qbx_core's 3D text, or /ooc comes twice
docs.text: In the chat box, the chat's channel commands always go to tobs_chat. If you still see qbx_core's 3D text, check that the channel isn't set to enabled = false in config.lua, and that the chat was opened with T (typing me in the F8 console can reach qbx_core's command instead).

docs.title: Join and quit lines show twice, or in another style
docs.text: qbx_chat_theme sends its own join and quit lines. Remove it (it only styles the default chat), or keep it and tobs_chat skips its own.

docs.title: A script's messages don't show
docs.text: Scripts written for the default chat work unchanged. Check the F8 console for errors from that script, and that tobs_chat starts before it in server.cfg (where ensure chat was).

docs.title: "You can't use /pd" or "Go on duty to use /pd"
docs.text: The player needs the job in the channel's jobs (with at least that grade) and, with onDuty = true, to be on duty. After a setjob it takes up to 2 seconds.

docs.title: The console says "channel /pd can't be used"
docs.text: A job channel needs a framework: tobs_chat didn't find qbx_core. Check that qbx_core runs, or set Config.Framework to 'qbox'. A channel with a mistake in config.lua shows "Config.Channels[n] (...) is off" with the reason, and is left out.

docs.title: There are no tabs above the chat
docs.text: Tabs only show for players who can use a radio or the staff channel (mode = true). A civilian sees none.

docs.title: The rank doesn't show on /pd
docs.text: rank = true takes the grade name from the job's grades in qbx_core/shared/jobs.lua. A grade without a name shows no rank.

docs.title: Staff commands say "Only staff can do that"
docs.text: Give the ace in server.cfg and restart: add_ace group.admin tobs_chat.staff allow. The player must be in that group.

docs.title: Nothing arrives in Discord
docs.text:
• Set the webhook with set tobs_chat:webhook "..." in server.cfg (set, not setr), and restart.
  • Config.Logs.discord must be true.
  • Logs are sent in batches every 5 seconds, so wait a moment.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Ask on Discord with your Qbox version, what you did, and what the F8 and server consoles show.
